tagline.text: An old town at the gateway to Panglao Island, with the Assumption church and Hinagdanan Cave

location.label: Location
location.text: Poblacion, Dauis, Bohol (northern Panglao Island, about 3 km across the bridge from Tagbilaran)

tags.label: Tags
items: Church of Our Lady of the Assumption

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱200–1,500 (half day, covering fees, tricycles and meals)

children.text: Dauis is an old town on the north of Panglao Island, the first place you reach after crossing the bridge from Tagbilaran, and it has a 17th-century Church of Our Lady of the Assumption and Hinagdanan Cave. It lies on the way to the Panglao beaches, so even a half-day stop on the way is rewarding.
Dauis is a municipality on the north of Panglao Island, about
3 km

from Bohol's provincial capital, Tagbilaran. It is linked to Tagbilaran by bridges and a causeway, and that road continues to where the Panglao beach resorts cluster. According to the 2024 census it has about 53,900 residents in 12 barangays, with names such as Dao, Biking, Mariveles and Totolan on the map. It is easy to pass through on the way to the airport or Alona Beach, but it is one of the oldest towns in Bohol, and Chinese artifacts are said to have been found here in the 1970s. Today it is a first-class municipality and one of the residential and commercial areas of fast-growing Panglao Island, so shops and restaurants line the road.

The symbol of the town is the Church of Our Lady of the Assumption (Dauis Church). It is said to have been built by Spanish missionaries in the 17th century, though accounts of when it was built differ. The magnitude 7.2 Bohol earthquake of October 15, 2013 brought down the facade and part of the roof, and for more than three years parishioners heard Mass at a makeshift altar under a century-old acacia tree. After restoration work in which the National Historical Commission (NHCP) spent about ₱33.74 million, the church reopened on
August 15, 2017
, the feast of the Assumption.

Beneath the altar is a small well. Devotees say it appeared when people who had taken shelter in the church during a siege of the town were suffering without water, and they believe its water has healing power. Whether the attackers were pirates or the Dutch depends on who tells the story, and it remains local tradition. The well is still said to be a source of water for people living near the church. The town's history runs deep in other ways too. According to Wikipedia, Dauis was part of the old Bo-ol chiefdom, the parish was formally established by 1697 (sources differ on whether the founders were Jesuits or Augustinians), and a stone watchtower said to have been built in 1774 survives as ruins. Most town records were lost during World War II.

Hinagdanan Cave, near the church, is famous for its turquoise underground lagoon, and on the coast there is a well-known restaurant, Bohol Bee Farm. Everything is close together, so it is easy to put together a half-day, and it fits most efficiently on the day you enter or leave Panglao. Because Dauis lies on the way from Tagbilaran toward Panglao, it is also natural to see the church first on the afternoon you arrive at Tagbilaran port and then move on to Panglao. If you are short of time, you can cut it to 20–30 minutes at the church and move on to the cave; if you have time to spare, you can have lunch at Bohol Bee Farm and rest while looking at the sea. Either way, bring a little cash, and remember that both the church and the cave are places of faith and nature, so move around quietly.

blocks.title: Church of Our Lady of the Assumption

children.text: This is the face of Dauis. Inside the restored stone church you can see the well beneath the altar and worshippers at prayer. On the feast of the Assumption,
August 15

, there is a large Mass and procession and the town is at its liveliest. It is polite to cover your shoulders and knees. Many people say the community's perseverance is more moving than the building itself, since the church was restored after more than three years of Mass at a temporary altar following the 2013 earthquake. Once you know its restoration and history, the same building looks different.

A small well that devotees believe holds miraculous water. The stories include episodes of people escaping pirates or an invasion, and the exact origin cannot be confirmed, but it is a place the townspeople still cherish, so look around quietly.

The name means "cave with a ladder," and it is said that a farmer found it while clearing land and went down on a ladder. Past the narrow entrance you find large stalagmites and stalactites lit by light through holes in the ceiling, and a turquoise lagoon. The lagoon is a mix of fresh and sea water, bats live in the cave so there is a smell, and the number of people allowed in at one time is said to be limited to 50. The cave is also said to have been a refuge for local people during World War II. Paths run between the stalagmites and stalactites, so watch your step and walk slowly. Ask at the entrance whether you can get help from the local staff.
There is a separate swimming fee in addition to the entrance fee, and swimming is allowed until
. There are also warnings that bat droppings can make the water less clean than it looks, so if that bothers you, just take photos and leave.
An organic restaurant and inn set along a coastal cliff, famous for serving malunggay (moringa) ice cream in a cone. Entry itself is said to be free, but tours and workshops cost extra.
The Bohol tourism office lists Bikini Beach and Bingag Beach as sights near Hinagdanan Cave. How wide the sand is and whether you can swim depend on the tide and the season, so check locally.

It is said that a bridge was built in the Spanish period, and today modern bridges and a causeway link Dauis with Tagbilaran. The coastal drive, which looks different with the tide, is part of the pleasure of heading into Panglao.
Leave your hotel in Tagbilaran or Panglao and arrive at Dauis Church. Early is better for photos, with soft light.
Quietly look around the inside of the church and the well beneath the altar.
Take a tricycle to Hinagdanan Cave, pay the entrance fee and see the cave.
If you like, pay the swimming fee and swim in the lagoon.
Have lunch at a restaurant on the coast.
In the afternoon you can continue to Alona Beach or Balicasag Island. If you swim in the cave your clothes will be wet, so leave a change of clothes and a towel in the car.

items.title: Airport and port transfer day route
items.subtitle: A short stop

children.text: Leave your bags at your hotel, see the church first and move on.
See the cave and then cross over toward Panglao.
There are direct flights from Manila to Bohol-Panglao International Airport (TAG). Airlines and schedules change, so check when you book.
You can also take a high-speed ferry from Cebu to Tagbilaran.
Check the latest announcements for flight and ferry schedules.
Take a jeepney or shared van from the Dao Integrated Bus Terminal toward Panglao or Dauis and you arrive in about
15–20 minutes
. Get off at the Dauis poblacion or on Bingag Road.
By motorcycle taxi it takes about
20–30 minutes
from Tagbilaran.
It is a short distance from central Tagbilaran to Dauis Church, so you can also go by tricycle or taxi.
It is about
2.5 km
from Dauis to Hinagdanan Cave, and a tricycle is the main way to get there. One source says it is around ₱150–200 from hotels to the cave.
If you charter a vehicle, it is easy to cover the church, the cave and a restaurant in one go.
The church and the cave can be visited all year, and the
December–May
dry season is easiest for getting around, but the cave is indoors, so you can keep your plans even when it rains.
Around the Assumption feast on
August 15
and the fiesta on
the last Sunday of January
the town is at its liveliest, but also crowded.

Mornings are best. Guides say the cave is less crowded and cooler in the morning, and the church is quiet if you avoid Mass times. In the hot months of March–May, visit the cave before lunch and rest in an air-conditioned restaurant in the afternoon.

On the coast toward Panglao, Dauis has resorts such as Bohol Bee Farm, as well as guesthouses and restaurants, and lodging continues all the way to Alona Beach as you go deeper into Panglao. It is 15–30 minutes by car from Tagbilaran, so access is easy wherever you stay. Bohol Bee Farm also runs accommodations, and one source says it has 38 air-conditioned rooms.

The Bohol Bee Farm restaurant is known as a place to enjoy organic salads and malunggay ice cream while looking at the sea from a cliff; sources differ on its opening hours, so check before you go. In the town center, small restaurants serve Bohol home cooking.

In the evening, it is common to cross to Tagbilaran and eat at a restaurant in the city, or to eat seafood at a coastal restaurant toward Panglao. Before you move on to Panglao, it helps to buy water and snacks at a shop or convenience store along the road in Dauis.
Visit the church at a quiet time, away from Mass, and cover your shoulders and knees.
The cave is less crowded and cooler in the morning.
If you want to swim, bring swimwear, a towel, a waterproof bag, a change of clothes and cash.
The cave entrance is narrow and steep, so wear shoes that do not slip.
There is a note that carrying an ID may qualify you for a discounted rate.
Agree the charter fee with the tricycle driver first and include waiting for the round trip.
For the latest information about the town, check with the municipal tourism office and the Bohol tourism office.
The church and the cave are close together, so one tricycle charter makes it easy to see both.
If a guide or staff member helps you at the cave, it is customary to give a small tip.
General tourist-area precautions such as watching for pickpockets apply here too, so keep valuables in front of you.
The water in Hinagdanan Cave may be less clean than it looks because of bat droppings and the like, and the entrance is narrow and steep. Think carefully before deciding to swim.
Only 50 people are said to be allowed in the cave at one time.
The cave smells of bats, so people who are sensitive should bring a mask.
The church well is an object of faith, so ask permission before taking photos and follow the instructions about drinking from it or touching it.
Fees and hours change often, so check the latest information locally.
Wear a life jacket when swimming in the cave lagoon.
Cross the bridge and the island continues, with beach resorts including Alona Beach.
The signature beach in the south of Panglao Island, about
30 minutes
by car from Dauis.
Bohol's provincial capital, about
3 km
across the bridge, with restaurants and terminals.
